title: Chile: History & Governance Update — Wed Aug 26, 2026
summary: Kast's ACOT constitutional security reform, signed August 10 to create a new 240-day presidential state of exception, drew mounting cross-partisan backlash through late August. Cadem polling shifted from 58% opposed to unilateral presidential power (Aug 20) to 49% opposed with Kast's disapproval at 57% (Aug 24). On August 25, Senate President Paulina Núñez — from Kast's own Renovación Nacional — publicly called to withdraw the state-of-exception clause for lacking coalition votes; the government dropped the bill's legislative fast-track, and Kast pressed his coalition for political backing at a PDI vehicle-delivery ceremony the same day, where a separate poll put his disapproval at 57.6%.

title: Chile: History & Governance Update — May 24, 2026
summary: Chile's Chamber of Deputies passed the base text of President Kast's flagship economic reconstruction bill 90-59-1 on May 20, cutting the corporate tax rate from 27% to 23% — but the contested 25-year tax stability clause faces an uncertain path in the Senate. In parallel, a joint Army-Carabineros-PDI operation arrested Mapuche werkén Jorge Huenchullán at Temucuicui by helicopter on May 19; a Collipulli court ordered preventive detention on May 20 with prosecutors seeking 18 years. The Huenchullán family issued a formal denunciation on May 23 accusing the state of a 'racist structure' that criminalizes the community. A Codelco internal audit revealed a 27,000-tonne production overstatement — the state copper giant's true 2025 output is the lowest since 1998 — with an executive fired and $14.3 million in bonuses clawed back. Q1 2026 GDP contracted 0.5% as copper output fell 5.8%. Kast's approval fell to approximately 26% on Day 70, with 66% of Chileans skeptical the reform will revive the economy.
